parts.title: Section 3
parts.passageHtml:
{[A.][250571]} {[Despite its obvious connection, mass production was not a corollary to the modern Industrial Revolution.][250573]} {[Various mass production techniques had been practiced in ancient times, from ceramic production in the Orient to manufacturing in ancient Greece.][250588]} {[The British were most likely the first modern economy to adapt water-powered, then steam-powered, machinery to industrial production methods, most notably in the textiles industry.][250610]} {[Yet it is generally agreed that modern mass production techniques came into widespread use through the innovation of an assortment of Americans who substantially improved the ancient techniques.][250636]} {[Indeed, this modern mass production was called the American System and its early successes are often attributed to Eli Whitney, who adapted mass production techniques and the interchangeability of parts to the manufacture of muskets for the U. S. government in the late 1790s.][250664]}

{[B.][250709]} {[In the late 18th century, French General Jean-Baptiste Vaquette de Gribeauval, promoted standardized weapons, which became known as the Systeme Gribeauval after it was issued as a royal order in 1765.][250711]} {[(Its focus at the time was artillery more than muskets or handguns. )][250742]} {[The crucial step toward interchangeability in metal parts was taken by Simeon North, working only a few miles from Eli Terry.][250754]} {[North created one of the world‘s first true milling machines to do metal shaping that previously was done by hand with a file.][250775]} {[Diana Muir believes that North‘s milling machine was online around 1816.][250798]} {[While Whitney was certainly an innovator of the American System, others maintain that Whitney‘s parts were not truly interchangeable and that credit should more appropriately go to John Hall, the New England gunsmith who built Muskets with flintlock for the United States government at the Harper‘s Ferry armory.][250811]} {[Flintlock, as it was implied meant people used it to trigger the gun.][250860]} {[Hall, born in Maine in 1769, built many of the machine tools needed for precision manufacturing and instituted a system that employed accurate gauges for measuring every aspect and piece of work his factory produced.][250874]} {[Consequently, he achieved a much higher level of interchangeability and precision than did Whitney.][250909]}

{[C. Still others maintain that the credit for these modem innovations should go to a French gunsmith whose methods and results predated those of Whitney and Hall by at least a decade.][250924]} {[In Britain, and somewhat simultaneously with Whitney, the Frenchman Marc Isambard Brunei adapted steam-driven machinery and assembly-line techniques to the production of 130,000 pulleys for the marine industry in just one year.][250955]} {[Brunei‘s achievements were made possible by the design and manufacture of several machine tools by the noted British inventor, Henry Maudslay.][250988]}

{[D. Maudslay‘s contribution to modem mass production was the invention of precision machine tools capable of producing the identical parts necessary for mass production techniques which made producing guns cheaper.][251012]} {[ It is generally conceded that the British machine tool industry was far more advanced than that of the Americans in these early stages of mass production development.][251044]} {[Simultaneous with Whitney‘s innovations in the United States were those of Oliver Evans, whose many inventions in the flour milling process led to an automated mill that could be run by a single miller.][251072]}

{[E. Samuel Colt and Elisha King Root were also very successful innovators in the development of industrial processes that could mass produce interchangeable parts for the assembly-line production of firearms.][251107]} {[Colt and Root wished to advance the machining of parts so that even the most minute of tasks could be performed with the precision that they believed only machines could achieve.][251138]} {[In these endeavors, Colt and Root were largely successful.][251149]}

{[F. Eli Terry also adapted mass production methods to clockmaking in the early 1800s, and George Eastman made innovations to assembly-line techniques in the manufacture and the developing of photographic film later in the century.][251161]} {[Credit for the development of large scale, assembly-line, mass production techniques is usually given to Henry Ford and his innovative Model T production methods.][251197]} {[Henry Ford had his workers standing in one place while parts were brought by on conveyor belts, and the car itself moved past the workers on another conveyor belt.][251222]} {[Bodies were built on one line and the chassis and drive train were built on another.][251252]} {[When both were essentially complete, the body was lowered onto the chassis for final assembly.][251269]} {[ Around the same time, production of guns also entered into the assembly line.][251285]}

{[G. Despite the fact that he was not the first, Ford can certainly be viewed as the most successful of these early innovators due to one simple fact– Ford envisioned and fostered mass consumption as a corollary to mass production.][251300]} {[Ford‘s techniques lessened the time needed to build a Model T from about twelve and a half hours to an hour and a half; the price was reduced as well–from $850 for the first Model T in 1908, to only $290 in 1927 after assembly-line techniques were introduced in 1913.][251342]} {[The automobile was no longer a luxury for the rich, the Model T fast became a necessity for nearly everyone.][251392]} {[Indeed, Ford sold almost half of all of the automobiles bought worldwide from 1908 to 1927–the years of Model T production.][251411]} {[Apart from this, people showed different views over whether guns should be involved in mass production.][251433]} {[ The expense opposition to ammunition was the first one to trigger the debate.][251450]} {[Other equipment involved in war or preparation for war was also against.][251464]} {[Let alone all these required a lot of workforce to accomplish.][251476]}

{[H. Assembly-line techniques also required that the manual skills necessary to build a product be altered.][251499]} {[Previous to mass production techniques, as seen in the early manufacture of firearms, each workman was responsible for the complete manufacture and assembly of all of the component parts needed to build any single product.][251515]} {[Mass production and parts interchangeability demanded that all parts be identical and the individual worker no longer be allowed the luxury of building a complete product based on his personal skills and inclinations.][251551]} {[Machines came to dictate the production process, and each part–once created individually by hand–was now duplicated by a machine process that was merely guided by human control.][251584]} {[The craft tradition, dominant in human endeavor for centuries, was abandoned in favor of a process that created parts by machine.][251613]} {[Furthermore, assembly of these machine-made parts was divided into a series of small repetitive steps that required much less skill than traditional craftsmanship.][251634]} {[Consequently, modern mass production techniques, while certainly increasing the efficiency of the manufacturing process and bringing industrial products within the reach of virtually all of humanity, apart from manufacturing ballpoint pens, making of gun is also part of it.][251657]} {[But safety is also a factor to consider.][251697]} {[People succeeded in restrain the production of guns resulting only 4 manufactures were permitted to produce guns in mass production.][251705]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 1 - 6:

The reading passage has eight paragraphs, A-H. Choose the correct heading for paragraphs C-H from the list below.

Write the correct number, i-viii, in boxes 1-6 on your answer sheet.

List of Headings

i      The appearance of precision machine tools

ii     Different techniques applied to mass production

iii    Prominent researchers‘ work dedicated to mass production of firearm making

iv    The disagreement on the first person who invented real interchangeable parts instead of Whitney

v     Successful elements for imposing restrictions on the production of guns

vi    Controversy on the permission of guns production

vii   The use of mass production to manufacture guns

viii  The significant role of interchangeable parts

questions.explanationHtml:
IV

 

“The disagreement on the first person who invented real interchangeable parts instead of Whitney”: Sự bất đồng về người đầu tiên sáng chế ra các phần có thể thay thế nhau thay vì Whitney

 

Giải thích: Thông tin ở đoạn B cho biết người sáng chế ra các mảnh có thể thay thế lẫn nhau (interchangeable parts) có thể là Whitney hoặc Hall, nhưng đoạn C cho biết nhiều người cho rằng phát minh đổi mới này là công của một người thợ làm súng (gunsmith) người Pháp tên là Marc Isambard Brunei

I

 

“The appearance of precision machine tools”: Sự xuất hiện của các máy móc với độ chính xác

 

Giải thích: Đóng góp của Maudslay cho việc sản xuất hàng loạt hiện đại là phát minh về các máy móc hoạt động với độ chính xác (precision) để sản xuất các phần cần thiết cho dây chuyền sản xuất hàng loạt, việc đã giúp sản xuất súng trở nên rẻ hơn

III

 

“prominent researchers‘ work dedicated to mass production of firearm making”: Công trình của các nhà nghiên cứu nổi bật đóng góp vào việc sản xuất hàng loại các vũ khí

 

Giải thích: Hai nhà nghiên cứu Colt và Root đã thành công trong việc phát triển các quy trình công nghiệp giúp sản xuất hàng loạt các mảnh có thể thay thế nhau cho dây chuyền sản xuất súng

II

 

“Different techniques applied to mass production”: Những kĩ thuật khác nhau được áp dụng vào sản xuất hàng loạt

 

Giải thích: Các kĩ thuật sản xuất hàng (mass production techniques) loạt được cho là công của Henry Ford. Ông cho nhân viên của mình đứng yên một chỗ trong khi các phần của xe hơi được đưa tới chỗ nhân viên thông qua các băng tải (conveyor belts). Các bộ phận của khung xe (bodies) được lắp ở một băng, còn phần gầm (chassis) và hệ thống truyền động (drive train) được lắp ở một băng khác. Khi phần khung xe được lắp xong, phần này sẽ tự được hạ xuống để lắp vào phần gầm → đây chính là các kĩ thuật được ứng dụng cho sản xuất hàng loạt

VI

 

“Controversy on the permission of guns production”: Tranh cãi về quyền sản xuất súng

 

Giải thích: Người ta có nhiều ý kiến trái chiều (different views) về việc súng có nên được đưa vào sản xuất hàng loạt không

V

 

“Successful elements for imposing restrictions on the production of guns”: Những yếu tố thành công trong việc hạn chế việc sản xuất súng

 

Giải thích: Người ta đã thành công trong việc hạn chế sản xuất súng, kết quả là chỉ có 4 nhà sản xuất được phép sản xuất súng hàng loạt

Questions 7 - 9:

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

Write your answers in boxes 7-9 on your answer sheet.

questions.explanationHtml:
7

C


“Fire the gun”: Khai nòng súng


Giải thích: “Flintlock” được người ta dùng để khai hỏa (trigger the gun)

options.text: To demonstrate that mass production needed detailed techniques
To show that every object could be detached into several parts
To emphasize that Ford was a successful enterprise
To stress that cars were popular at that time in the U.S.

questions.explanationHtml:
8

Đoạn F

"Henry Ford had his workers standing in one place while parts were brought by on conveyor belts, and the car itself moved past the workers on another conveyor belt. Bodies were built on one line and the chassis and drive train were built on another. When both were essentially complete, the body was lowered onto the chassis for final assembly"

=> Câu B

Giải thích: Ở đây, tác giả đưa ra ví dụ về quy trình sản xuất hàng loạt của Henry Ford vì trong đó, mỗi chiếc xe được hình thành từ nhiều thành phần và mỗi 1 thành phần được cấu tạo từ nhiều bộ phận nhỏ khác

=> Cho thấy mọi vật đều có thể được tháo dỡ thành nhiều phần

options.text: Introduced assembly line for producing interchangeable parts of guns
Created useful tools for manufacture of guns with economic feasibility
Lessened the time for making guns
Set a standard of making guns and the standard of interchangeable parts

questions.explanationHtml:
9

B


“Created useful tools for manufacture of guns with economic feasibility”: Tạo ra những công cụ hữu ích cho sản xuất súng với tính khả thi về mặt kinh tế


Giải thích: Maudslay đã sáng chế ra các máy móc hoạt động với độ chính xác, từ đó giúp sản xuất ra các phần tương tự nhau được dùng cho quy trình sản xuất hàng loạt, từ đó làm việc sản xuất súng trở nên rẻ hơn → khả thi về mặt kinh tế

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Question 13:

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

Write your answers in box 13 on your answer sheet.

options.text: The origin of auto assembly line
A marvelous advancement in firearm production
The significance of producing interchangeable parts

questions.explanationHtml:
13

C


“The origin of mass production”: Nguồn gốc của sản xuất hàng loạt


Giải thích: Các thông tin trong đoạn từ A đến F cho rất nhiều câu chuyện về cách mà sản xuất hàng loạt (mass production) ra đời → tiêu đề phù hợp cho cả passage này là “the origin of mass production)
